documents.text: Now, therefore, we shall expound the nature of supreme devotional love (Bhakti).
That devotion is of the nature of supreme, unconditional love for the Divine.
And it is of the nature of immortality, freeing the seeker from all mortal fears.

documents.sanskrit: यल्लव्ध्वा पुमान् सिद्धो भवत्यमृतो भवति तृप्तो भवति
documents.transliteration: Yal-labdhva puman siddho bhavaty amrito bhavati tripto bhavati
documents.text: Attaining which a human being becomes spiritually perfected, immortal, and utterly contented.

documents.sanskrit: यत्प्राप्य न किञ्चिद् वाञ्छति न शोचति न द्वेष्टि न रमते नोत्साही भवति
documents.transliteration: Yat prapya na kinchid vanchhati na shochati na dveshti na ramate notsahi bhavati
documents.text: Attaining which one no longer craves worldly objects, neither grieves nor hates, nor delights in ephemeral pleasures, nor strives for selfish gain.
Narada holds that Bhakti consists of dedicating all everyday actions to the Divine, and experiencing profound inner longing whenever remembrance of the Divine is forgotten.
The true nature of divine love is ineffable, beyond the capacity of words to fully convey.
It is like the taste of sweet nectar experienced by one who cannot speak—deeply felt within the heart, though silent to the world.
